defects_closed.defect: PKCS7_dataInit read the cipher-reported IV and key lengths and wrote them into fixed [u8; 16] / [u8; 64] stack buffers through RAND_bytes_ex and EVP_CIPHER_CTX_rand_key.
defects_closed.fix: Refuse ivlen > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH and keylen > EVP_MAX_KEY_LENGTH with PKCS7_DOIT_CIPHER_LENGTH_REFUSED before either write; every length that fits keeps the authority's control flow.
defects_closed.class: UB in the C authority not reproduced (AGENTS.md section 17); reachable at the C ABI, not from parsed PKCS#7 alone.

defects_closed.defect: Twelve PKCS7_dataInit failure paths leaked an already-built BIO filter chain: the digest chain was a bare pointer released only on the single success-adjacent tail, and the cipher filter was released alone.
defects_closed.fix: OwnedChain (Drop = BIO_free_all) owns the chain under construction and a second owner holds the cipher filter until the success path links it; BIO_free_all expressions in PKCS7_dataInit went 8 -> 0.

defects_closed.defect: CMS_add0_recipient_password wrote a cipher-reported IV length into a fixed [u8; 16] buffer through RAND_bytes_ex and then handed it to EVP_EncryptInit_ex.
defects_closed.fix: Refuse ivlen > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH with CMS_PWRI_IV_REFUSED before the write; reachable at the C ABI through a METH/provider cipher, not from parsed DER alone.
defects_closed.class: UB in the C authority not reproduced (AGENTS.md section 17).

defects_closed.defect: kek_wrap_key read in[0..3] as the RFC 3211 header without proving three bytes were readable; with a block size of 1-4 and a 0-2 byte input the length checks did not imply inlen >= 3.
defects_closed.fix: Refuse inlen < 3 before the round-up and before any pointer use; use checked_add/checked_mul for the round-up and refuse a non-positive block size before casting.
defects_closed.class: internal-boundary out-of-bounds read; C-ABI reachable with a custom KEK cipher and a short content key.

defects_closed.defect: tls13_psk_do_binder read hashsize bytes through a bare *const u8 supplied from an attacker-length ClientHello binder, so a valid ticket with a 1-byte binder caused an out-of-bounds read.
defects_closed.fix: The received binder is a &[u8] and the compare requires received.len() == hashsize; the caller also refuses a resolved-ticket binder of the wrong length with the authority's DECODE_ERROR/BAD_EXTENSION and bounds the transcript offset.
defects_closed.class: attacker-reachable out-of-bounds read from the wire; fixed.

defects_closed.defect: The ClientHello extension walk published SNI, ALPN, status type, PHA and peer sigalgs as each extension was reached, so a later malformed extension left partial state published on a rejected hello; truncations were silently accepted and lengths were computed by hand.
defects_closed.fix: A two-pass safe parse over &[u8] returns Result<ParsedExtensions, HelloReject> and never touches Ssl; one unsafe commit_client_hello publishes only after the whole block and callback succeed; every reject goes through one ossl_statem_fatal closure that poisons the state machine with the authority's alert/reason. 15 malformed cases covered.
defects_closed.class: state-preservation and unchecked-length elimination; OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED.

defects_closed.defect: SSL_CTX_add_session's eviction arm invoked the application removal callback while holding ctx.lock; the crate's CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock reports recursive acquisition as failure, so a callback that re-entered the cache silently failed.
defects_closed.fix: Detach every entry, unlock, then invoke the removal callback and release the detached reference outside the lock; the callback is snapshotted so a retiring context is not re-read.
defects_closed.class: reentrancy edge (AGENTS.md section 21); deliberate safety divergence from the authority's lock-held callback.

defects_closed.defect: Insert evicted size-cap entries before the push that could refuse, so a refused push removed live entries and was not failure-atomic; the replacement arm released the incumbent before the push.
defects_closed.fix: Push first, then replace the incumbent and evict down to session_cache_size; a refused push returns 0 with the cache unchanged.

defects_closed.defect: Last-reference releases (application ex_data destructors) ran under ctx.lock for both the replaced incumbent and each evicted entry.
defects_closed.fix: Release every detached cache reference after unlock.
defects_closed.class: reentrancy edge (ex_data callback under a non-recursive lock).

defects_closed.defect: SSL_SESS_CACHE_UPDATE_TIME was applied only to new entries, so re-adding a cached session did not refresh its expiry as the authority does.
defects_closed.fix: Update time and recalculate the timeout unconditionally after the same-key decision.

defects_closed.defect: A negative SSL_CTX_flush_sessions cutoff was cast to u64 and flushed the entire cache; the authority's signed comparison expires nothing for t < 0.
defects_closed.fix: Compare the signed cutoff so only t == 0 flushes everything.

defects_closed.defect: The authority's every-255-connections automatic cache flush was not modelled, so a long-lived context never expired sessions automatically.
defects_closed.fix: Implement the authority trigger, counter and SSL_CTX_flush_sessions_ex call, including its no-op error behaviour.

defects_closed.defect: TLS1.2 DHE client key exchange failed. Four causes: SSL_R_BAD_SIGNATURE was defined as 148 (SSL_R_DH_PUBLIC_VALUE_LENGTH_IS_WRONG) instead of 123; tls12_verify did not implement the rsa_pss_rsae/pss or DSA signature schemes; extended_master_secret was advertised but neither the server echo nor RFC 7627's session-hash master secret was implemented; and tls12_process_server_key_exchange had no SSL_kDHE arm at all.
defects_closed.fix: Implement the DHE arm with checked p/g/Ys parsing, big-endian BN import (OSSL_PARAM_construct_BN is native-endian), param/public checks, security-bits check and signature verification; add the PSS/DSA schemes and correct SSL_R_BAD_SIGNATURE to 123; record the EMS echo and derive the RFC 7627 master secret; add the DHE GCM suites.
defects_closed.class: implementation defect with an attacker-visible parity failure; the negative-control canary is an ECDHE-only reader refusing the DHE frame.

Release preparation for 0.0.34: version bump, Phase-2 rebuild (libcrypto defe179f / libssl 5066aa32), 11/11 ABI courts, cargo package verification and documentation regeneration. 0.0.34 was then published. A version bump is not a re-measurement: no downstream row was re-run.

PKCS#7 dataInit hardened: cipher-reported IV/key lengths are refused before writing into the fixed 16/64-byte stack buffers, and the twelve BIO filter-chain leak paths are consolidated into OwnedChain (8 BIO_free_all expressions -> 0). FAST only; BATCH and SEAL NOT_RUN.

CMS PWRI hardened: an oversized KEK IV is refused before RAND_bytes_ex, and kek_wrap_key refuses inlen < 3 before reading the RFC 3211 header; the round-up uses checked arithmetic. FAST only; BATCH and SEAL NOT_RUN.

Server ClientHello extension block rebuilt as a state-preserving two-pass safe parse with one commit point and authority-shaped fatal rejects; 15 malformed cases covered. The TLS1.3 PSK binder out-of-bounds read is fixed by requiring received.len() == hashsize. OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED; FAST only.

Session cache: six defects closed, including application removal/ex_data callbacks invoked under a non-recursive cache lock (now detached and run unlocked), non-failure-atomic insert (push before eviction), UPDATE_TIME on re-add, the signed flush cutoff, and the every-255-connection auto-flush. Eight cache-lifecycle tests include end-to-end TLS1.2 resumption. FAST only.

Downstream re-measurement with evidence_reuse=null over the 166 loaded families: 157 candidate / 157 authority L7, below_baseline=0, no lost or gained family. The 157-family claim is rebound to the install built at 03ff4327d (libcrypto 2b0ff1b6 / libssl f99f7159).

Working tree moved to 0.0.35 because published 0.0.34 predates S27-S32. Rebuilt libcrypto 61373488 / libssl cd24d207 deterministically, ran 11/11 ABI courts, and rebound the atlas identity with candidate_identity_match=false; 157/157 is explicitly not a 0.0.35 measurement. No publish.

Corpus batch 1: 25 new recipes -> 191 recipes, 179 loaded, 169 L7; recipe/tool defects fixed. One IMPLEMENTATION gap found: perl-net-ssleay TLS1.2 DHE fails with SSL_R_DH_PUBLIC_VALUE_LENGTH_IS_WRONG. No src/ change.

TLS1.2 DHE client defect fixed. Four causes: SSL_R_BAD_SIGNATURE defined as 148 instead of 123; no RSA-PSS/DSA signature verification; no extended-master-secret derivation; and no SSL_kDHE arm in tls12_process_server_key_exchange. Full library suite 2089 passed / 0 failed / 44 ignored; fmt, clippy --lib and 11/11 ABI courts green; BOUNDARY/SEAL NOT_RUN.

Downstream re-measurement with evidence_reuse=null over 191 recipe families at libcrypto 64dec4c7 / libssl b258b12f: candidate 169 L7, authority 170, below_baseline=1 (partclone, a consumer-side flake proven independent of the library). perl-net-ssleay rose L5->L7 after its session-resumption workload was corrected; 11/11 ABI courts; 191/191 build/link.

Corpus batch 2: ten Phase-1 workload repairs plus mutt -> 192 recipes, 183 loaded, 180 candidate = 180 authority L7, below_baseline=0, builds 191/191. Twelve families remain below L7 (eleven built/linked plus libcxxtools10) and 808 have no recipe. No src/ change; the Phase-2 addition is one family, reported as a shortfall rather than completion.

known_gaps.detail: The ml_dsa Vector typed-accessor-over-uninitialised-storage defect is closed by construction (PolyBlock zero-initialises before into_raw); S22 also closed the four sibling sites.
Vector::init / matrix_init remain safe raw-pointer constructors; the x509 policy-tree borrow and the provider cipher_gcm out-buffer slice formation remain retained obligations.

The only S33 IMPLEMENTATION gap (perl-net-ssleay TLS1.2 DHE/ECDHE) was repaired in S34; the family is L7-functional in S35/S36. No measured S36 family fails on the candidate after both subjects pass the same workload.
The only S17 IMPLEMENTATION-class downstream family (h2o/neverbleed legacy RSA dispatch) was repaired in S18 and is L7-functional in the current atlas.

charybdis reaches L5-loaded only. The workload drops to nobody with setpriv and the daemon reaches 'Server Ready', but its ssld TLS helper returns a handshake_failure alert for every client. No container capability was granted; the blocker is the environment, not the candidate.
fastd is L6-runtime because the court provides no /dev/net/tun and no CAP_NET_ADMIN (TUNSETIFF is refused), so its two-peer data path cannot run. It is not counted as a candidate failure.

Eight HARNESS and one FIXTURE family remain below L7 (coturn, gftp-text, gss-ntlmssp, krb5, libgit2, libmongocrypt, poco, libshout; FIXTURE: libengine-pkcs11-openssl). None is SOURCE_UNREACHABLE and every one is symmetric under both subjects.

Twelve families remain below L7: eleven built/linked (charybdis L5, fastd L6, libshout L5, and coturn/gftp-text/gss-ntlmssp/krb5/libengine-pkcs11-openssl/libgit2/libmongocrypt/poco at L4) plus libcxxtools10 at L2-configured because it does not compile. The blockers are ENVIRONMENT (charybdis, fastd, libcxxtools10), HARNESS (eight) and FIXTURE (libengine-pkcs11-openssl); none is attributed to src/.

partclone fell L7->L5 in S35 on a consumer-side S_ISBLK-on-uninitialised-stat ENOENT race; a ten-sample cross-matrix showed the failure does not track the crypto library (the authority binary also failed with authority libs and passed with candidate libs). The S36 workload now pre-creates the restore target through -O/--overwrite and the family is L7.

The S35 resumption fixture used SSL_get_session and freed the owning SSL/SSL_CTX before reuse, so the authority failed the marker too. Switching to SSL_get1_session and releasing it after the second connect made the family L7 under both subjects without weakening the marker.
808 of the 1000 counted families still have no admitted pristine-source recipe. They are acquire-failure / not-attempted rows, not candidate failures, and no URL is fabricated for them.

unsafe_count.counting_rule: occurrences of `unsafe {` plus `unsafe fn ` per file
unsafe_count.why_increased: S20 restored authority dispatch that had been deleted, and that code is made of calls to existing legacy-key accessors and method callbacks. Each added operation is an FFI call at an already-documented C-ABI/accessor boundary with an explicit SAFETY contract; no unsafe abstraction's contract was widened and six authority-UB paths were removed.
unsafe_count.classification: correctness win, not a safety regression: the operation count follows restored reachable behaviour, while the set of unsafe assumptions did not grow.
unsafe_count.note: This global count remains the S20 recount. S27-S34 record per-file before/after unsafe-operation counts in their receipts but no global recount was made; several changes relocated releases into owners (S27) or grouped existing calls into contracted blocks (S30) rather than adding abstractions.
